title: Quant Decision Matrix & Heuristics — prototype recommendation sheet
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working prototype for a decision matrix + heuristic ruleset that product and infra teams can use to pick a quantization target (INT8 / FP8 / 4-bit) for a given serving workload. Goal is to produce a small, easy-to-run spreadsheet and a short set of human-readable heuristics we can ship with Optimize as “starter recommendations.”

Audience:
- Eng/product owners who need quick guidance when onboarding a new model for serving
- Solutions engineers evaluating Dedicated/private deployments
- Optimize team building automated suggestions in the console

High-level summary:
- Deliverable: single-sheet spreadsheet (input rows = model+workload vectors) + 6 heuristic rules + example cost/latency/quality columns + calibration checklist.
- Inputs we expect: base model name, peak qps, p50 latency goal (ms), 99th percentile token length, quality sensitivity (acceptable BLEU/ROUGE/accuracy delta), memory constraints (GB), and whether KV cache sharing is possible.
- Outputs: recommended quant level (float32 / fp8 / int8 / 4-bit), expected cost multiplier vs baseline, expected median latency impact, expected quality delta band (low/medium/high), and confidence tag (high/medium/low).

Decision matrix (spreadsheet column suggestions):
- model_id: e.g., llama-2-13b, mixtral-8x8
- base_size_gb: baseline model size on GPU (float32)
- baseline_cost_per_1M_tokens_usd: current cost baseline (hosted pricing)
- qps_peak: requests per second (int)
- seq_length_p99: tokens per request (int)
- latency_slo_ms: desired p50 latency target (ms)
- quality_sensitivity: low|medium|high (user input)
- kv_cache_sharing: yes|no
- hw_type: a100/rtx/gh200/v100/etc
- candidate_quant: (list to evaluate) fp16 -> fp8 -> int8 -> 4bit
- est_cost_multiplier: spreadsheet formula estimate for each quant (see formulas)
- est_latency_pct_change: e.g., -5% to +20%
- est_quality_delta_pct: estimated output quality change vs fp16 baseline
- risk_notes: freeform
- recommendation: chosen quant level
- confidence: high/medium/low

Quick spreadsheet formulas (prototype):
- est_cost_multiplier = kernel_efficiency_factor(hw_type, candidate_quant) * memory_savings_factor(candidate_quant) * batch_utilization_factor(qps_peak, seq_length_p99)
  - kernel_efficiency_factor: table lookup; e.g., a100 fp8=0.85, int8=0.7, 4bit=0.55 (empirical; put in a separate tab).
  - memory_savings_factor: (1 - (bytes_per_param(candidate_quant) / bytes_per_param(fp16))). Example bytes: fp16=2, fp8=1, int8=1, 4bit=0.5.
  - batch_utilization_factor: e.g., if qps_peak allows batching to amortize RTT, multiplier reduces cost. Simple rule: if average batch size > 4 then *0.9, >8 then *0.8.

- est_latency_pct_change = kernel_latency_factor(candidate_quant) + overhead_from_quantize_dequantize(if using mixed execution)
  - kernel_latency_factor: table; fp8 can be slightly faster due to smaller memory traffic, int8 can be faster on optimized kernels but sometimes slower if fallback kernels used.

- est_quality_delta_pct: baseline quality - quantized_quality_estimate; express as small percentages or qualitative band.

Heuristic selection rules (ranked, applied in order):
1) Safety/Regulatory first: if model used for regulated PII-sensitive inference and private deployment requires bit-exact determinism, default to fp16/fp32. (Override)
2) If quality_sensitivity == high and any benchmarked delta > 0.5% absolute on target metric => pick fp8 or fp16.
3) If memory constraint (gpu_memory < base_size_gb * 0.6) => prefer 4-bit or int8; pick the smallest quant that keeps batch_size >= 1 for SLOs.
4) Latency-first workloads: if latency_slo_ms <= baseline_p50 * 0.9, pick faster quant variant per latency table; if none meet SLO, prefer model sharding or smaller model.
5) Cost-first workloads (quality_sensitivity == low and qps_peak > 50): default to int8, if int8 memory footprint still too large, consider 4-bit.
6) KV-cache heavy chat use-cases: avoid 4-bit for now unless we validate attention kernel stability; prefer int8 with KV sharing enabled.

Calibration & validation checklist (short runnable test plan):
- A/B eval harness: run 2000 samples from representative prompt set at baseline fp16 and each quant candidate, compute metric deltas (accuracy/ROUGE/BLEU/embedding-sim). Log p95/per-sample differences.
- Latency bench: synthetic qps ramp with seq lengths at p50/p95/p99, capture p50/p95 token latency.
- Memory/throughput: measure max batch size before OOM on target hw.
- Fallback plan: for any 4-bit candidate, include automated fallback to int8 if quality delta > threshold or variance in outputs > threshold.

Quality bands (prototype thresholds):
- low: <= 0.5% metric degradation (safe for many consumer apps)
- medium: 0.5% - 2% (acceptable for internal tools, search-ranking proxies)
- high: > 2% (risky for customer-facing quality-sensitive flows)

Example worked case (toy numbers):
- Model: redwood/gpt-like-7b, base_size_gb=28 (fp16), baseline_cost_per_1M_tokens_usd=120
- Workload: qps_peak=80, seq_p99=512, latency_slo_ms=180, quality_sensitivity=medium, hw_type=a100
- Candidate eval: fp8 -> est_cost_multiplier=0.78, est_latency_pct_change=-8%, est_quality_delta=0.6% (medium); int8 -> est_cost_multiplier=0.62, est_latency_pct_change=-12%, est_quality_delta=1.4% (medium); 4bit -> est_cost_multiplier=0.42, est_latency_pct_change=-20%, est_quality_delta=3.8% (high)
- Recommendation: int8 (confidence: medium) with canary at 5% traffic and the A/B eval harness running. Rationale: good cost win and latency improvement while quality degradation remains in medium band.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Need better kernel_efficiency table per hw; current numbers are placeholders from internal microbenchmarks. Get reorder from infra bench team.
- How to encode composite workloads (mixed short chat + long generation)? Consider weighted avg of batch_utilization and seq_length.
- Can we represent multi-quant hybrid (e.g., int8 weights + 4-bit activations) in the sheet? Probably add a hybrid column.
- Investigate FP8 variants (E4M3 vs E5M2) — quality/compat differences may matter for some architectures.

Next steps / TODOs:
- (Marco) pull kernel perf table from infra bench and populate the kernel_efficiency tab (due 2025-11-05).
- (Priya) run A/B harness on redwood/gpt-like-7b to get real quality deltas for int8 and 4-bit (due 2025-11-08).
- (Liam) prototype the single-sheet spreadsheet and add a "generate recommendation" formula cell that maps heuristic rules -> recommendation string (due 2025-11-12).
- Product: review default thresholds with solutions engineering and legal for regulated use-cases.

Appendix: quick paste of kernel table (editable tab in sheet):
- a100: fp8=0.85, int8=0.72, 4bit=0.5
- rtx4090: fp8=0.95, int8=0.88, 4bit=0.6
- gh200: fp8=0.8, int8=0.65, 4bit=0.46

End — this is intentionally concise; next revision should add: sample spreadsheet file (.xlsx) and a small CLI that takes JSON workload vectors and returns recommendation.

Unresolved: where to surface in Console: Optimize -> Suggestions vs Model page? Leaning toward both (Model page shows per-model quick rec; Optimize shows global cost impact).
